conservation.technical_description:
Overall the painting is in very good condition. It is unlined and on its original stretcher. The painting appears to have a spray application of a synthetic resin varnish, which imparts an overall gloss to the surface and saturation of colors. 
 
There is a green horizontal abrasion in the lower left corner with an associated brown accretion just above it. There is a loss in the flat gray paint near the abrasion as well as a loss to the impasto ridge just to the proper right of these issues. There is abrasion to the ground layer in the lower proper left corner. There are losses to several of the impasto ridges through the painting. Along the turnover edges there are remnants of silver leaf, likely from a previous frame. These are most noticeable along th bottom edge. There is some micro-cracking in the lower proper right corner, but it appears stable.

cr-1999:
Stretcher: inaccessible. Verso: inaccessible. Backing: 1. "3 Eggs in Pink Dish – 28?" (graphite) 2. OK {5star} (graphite) 3. "3 Eggs in Pink Dish / by Georgia O'Keeffe – / 1928?" (Andrew Droth, Label: printed, An American Place, black ink) 
(Source: Lynes, 1999)

remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Amer. Place, April 1946 . . . [note of backing inscription 1]. Initials. . . . Note: Same dish as in 'Pink Dish & Green Leaves at N.Y. Window' 1928." Whitney Archive indicates, "Three eggs in compote with pink top and white stem and base. White drapery." Dated 1928/1929 on basis of backing inscriptions 1, 3, and 1929 O'Keeffe letter. O'Keeffe wrote: "My latest is of eggs in a pink dish – three white eggs" (Georgia O'Keeffe to Catherine Klenert, 29 May 1929). (Source: Lynes, 1999)
